rows.grounds: compound vision of great vidyā lotus foot

items.question: What vision of the great vidyā's lotus foot is being approached equally?
premises: The verse names a vision of the great vidyā's lotus foot.
It pairs that vision with equal approach.
items.inference: The verse presents equal approach to the great vidyā's lotus-foot vision.
uncertainties: Exact verb root and sandhi of samavārupasi are not resolved.
items.plain_english: The vision of the great vidyā's lotus foot is approached equally.

premises: The verse states an intention to perform the wine rite.

uncertainties: Agent is implied from context.
items.plain_english: He went to the clan pavilion to perform the wine rite.

items.question: What did he become after accomplishing the rite again?

items.plain_english: Again and again, having accomplished it, he became a full yogin.

items.question: Who formerly worshipped Tārā at Nīlācala?

items.plain_english: Formerly a sage worshipped Tārā at Nīlācala.

uncertainties: Exact activity during those years is implied.
items.plain_english: Devoted to meditation, he spent ten thousand years.

items.question: What did Brahmā tell the sage to hear?
premises: Brahmā speaks to the sage.

uncertainties: The content of the word follows in later verses.
items.plain_english: Brahmā indeed said to the sage: hear, son, my word.

items.question: Whose auspicious feet should be worshipped with an unagitated mind?
premises: The verse commands worship.

uncertainties: The deity is implied from context.
items.plain_english: Worship the auspicious feet with an unagitated mind.

items.plain_english: I create the four Vedas and arrange them by play.

items.question: Who protects the world filled with truth-knowledge?

items.plain_english: Viṣṇu, filled with truth-knowledge, protects the world.

items.question: What happens when Tārā is well worshipped?

items.question: How was this hard-to-worship vidyā given to me by you?

items.plain_english: How was this hard-to-worship vidyā given to me by you?

items.plain_english: Even so, if the compassion of the crossing goddess was not in me.

items.question: What did the firm-vowed sage attain while without food?

items.plain_english: Having resorted to Kāmākhyā-yoni, he worshipped, O lord.

items.plain_english: Soon your success will be, no doubt.
